column1: # JSON SCHEMA EXPORT -- the bridge to every structured-output API.
# The review's finding I / SUPPORT.md act 2. Every major LLM provider's
# structured-output API constrains generation to JSON Schema and to
# nothing else, so without an export a model cannot ride that path and
# then be `vet`ted as the semantic gate -- and an MCP tool's
# `inputSchema`, which the protocol REQUIRES to be JSON Schema, cannot
# be derived from an aontu tool model at all.
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
# DIFFING. The expect object is the schema AND the loss report, because
# a schema that silently DROPPED a construct would look identical to one
# that carried it -- and a dropped constraint makes the schema admit
# MORE than the model does, which is the failure this language exists to
# refuse. The CLI's envelope (version, verb) is not compared.
# WHAT CROSSES EXACTLY: the string, boolean, null and number kinds and
# a fractional float literal; a disjunction of scalars to `enum`, its
# members deduplicated by JSON value and its preference to `default`; a
# disjunction of bare kinds to a `type` array; bounds to
# minimum/maximum, the OPEN endpoints as the exclusive keywords and an
# exact endpoint in its own digits; `re` to `pattern` in its normalised
# form, which is the ECMA-262 reading of what aontu means; `neq` of
# both leaves of a number to `not: {enum}`; `len` to the length, item
# or property counts, an open or fractional bound moved to the whole
# count inside it and an integer exclusion as `not`; `unique()` over a
# list of one leaf to uniqueItems; optional keys to an absence from
# `nil` to `false`; a conjunct of map templates to `allOf`; and -- the
# one aontu and JSON Schema say identically -- `close()` to
# `additionalProperties: <template>`, which is what it means; a written
# list is prefixItems for its positions and `items` for its spread, and
# `items: false` only when it is closed. A lone preference exports the
# kind its override admits, with the preferred value as `default`.
# WHAT DOES NOT, AND IS REPORTED: JSON reads 1 and 1.0 as one number and
# vet reads them as two leaves, so the integer and float kinds, a
# literal written in one leaf, a `neq` of one leaf and a `unique()` over
# a list that can hold two leaves of one number all differ from the
# schema; vet never reads JSON data as an exact leaf, so the `0d` kinds
# and literals differ too, though their digits are written exactly. A
# bound on a string (JSON Schema has no ordering keyword for strings),
# Schema has no uniqueness-by-property keyword), a hidden or type()
# entry (not generated, so not part of the value a consumer produces),
# a count with no domain, and any residue -- an unresolved reference is
# not a property constraint, and guessing one would be inventing a
# WHAT REFUSES THE RUN: a document that does not stand up, which is an
# unresolved reference, an anchor that names nothing, a failure nested
# anywhere in the exported value, or an atom whose arguments are
